solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Laughing about Romeo's crisp browned skin

indicators.note: the word for laughing goes around the other piece, as if surrounding it

parts.note: cackling is loud shrill laughing
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone guffaws over Romeo's crunchy roast skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Crackling is the crisp roasted rind of pork, a browned skin.

clue.text: Murderer I put in prison

indicators.note: the letter is placed inside the word for prison

parts.note: can is slang for a jail

explanation.surface: A killer confesses that they locked him up.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Abel's brother killed him, the first murderer in the Bible.

clue.text: Clothes appear to be tangled on line

indicators.note: getting tangled means the letters of appear are knotted into a new order

explanation.surface: Washing hung out seems knotted on the clothesline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be tangled' rearranges APPEAR into APPARE, then L is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal synonym for garments or attire.

clue.text: Japanese swimmer's a little flirtatious they say

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: coy means pretending to be shy in a mildly flirty way

explanation.surface: A Japanese swimmer is rumoured to be a bit of a flirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' signals a sound-alike: COY sounds like the fish's name.
explanation.definitionFit: These ornamental carp were bred in Japan and swim in garden ponds.

clue.text: Demand heroin sister's hiding

indicators.note: the phrase heroin sister's conceals the letters within it

explanation.surface: Someone demands to know where their sister is stashing heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hiding' points to the letters inside heroIN SISTer's.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to demand firmly, as a verb.

clue.text: Danger ape represented for occupant of pod?

indicators.note: presented again in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dangerous ape is depicted inside a space pod.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas grow inside pods, so a common garden variety lives in one.

clue.text: Fighting back? It might be bloody

indicators.note: read backwards, so the word for fighting runs the other way

parts.note: war is armed fighting

explanation.surface: A question about returning to combat, which may well get gory.
explanation.definitionFit: Raw meat, like a rare steak, is bloody; a raw wound may be too.

clue.text: Vicar out of bed. Prepare to move off?

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a vicar's title
up means risen from bed

explanation.surface: The vicar is up and about, ready to set off.
explanation.definitionFit: Drivers rev the engine up, raising its speed, before pulling away.

clue.text: Where to put money when everything's getting wet outside?

indicators.note: the word wet sits around the other piece

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Where to keep cash when the whole world is soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is only a link; the surface's rainy weather hides that wet is a container round the word for everything.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallet is the small folding case that holds banknotes and cards.

clue.text: Suggests one MP is telling tales

parts.note: the Roman numeral one is I
lies are tales told falsely

explanation.surface: Someone hints that a member of parliament is fibbing.
explanation.definitionFit: To imply is to suggest without saying outright, in the same third-person form.

clue.text: Celebrate in bar after retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a lever is a bar used to prise or lift

explanation.surface: Someone celebrates in a pub once they have retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub, but it is a crowbar.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel is to party and make merry, a synonym of celebrate.

clue.text: Do apple trees supply these shopkeepers?

indicators.note: read as supple, bending into shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about whether orchard trees stock the greengrocers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is read as an adverb from supple: bendily, so the letters bend into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradespeople is a collective term for shopkeepers and retailers.

clue.text: The arguments for maids?

definitions.meaning: a domestic is British slang for a household row, often one the police are called to
household servants, such as maids, are called domestic staff

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from domestic as household: a family quarrel, or a house servant.

clue.text: Very good fruit

explanation.definitionFit: A plum is the fruit, and figuratively an excellent or sought-after thing.

clue.text: Meet one's maker when in outskirts of Paris

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
the edges of the word Paris, its first and last letters

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

explanation.surface: Someone dies while on the edge of the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outskirts of' gives P and S, and 'in' puts AS between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass, or pass away, is a euphemism for dying, as is meeting one's maker.

clue.text: Inconsiderate son, a bit like a pixie

parts.note: elfish means resembling an elf, a pixie's cousin

explanation.surface: A thoughtless son is somewhat impish.
explanation.definitionFit: Selfish people put themselves first, without regard for others.

clue.text: Two bishops in river, getting bite from fish?

indicators.note: the bishops are placed inside the river

parts.note: the Nile is the great river of Egypt
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop, so two give BB

explanation.surface: A pair of clergymen angling in a river get a bite.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is fishing-themed: the bite is a fish's tentative one at the bait.
explanation.definitionFit: A nibble is a small tentative bite, as a fish takes at bait.

clue.text: Stuffy executive or potential husband?

parts.note: a suit is slang for a dull corporate manager

explanation.surface: Is the boring businessman a marriage prospect?
explanation.definitionFit: A suitor courts someone with marriage in mind, a would-be spouse.

clue.text: It's clear nuptial bed is disarranged

indicators.note: put out of order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Plainly, the wedding-night bed is in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disarranged' shuffles the letters of NUPTIAL BED IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond dispute or doubt is clear, obvious and certain.

clue.text: They say colouring's on the way out

indicators.note: signals that the word is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: dyeing is colouring fabric or hair

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that hair-tinting is going out of fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They say' signals a sound-alike: DYEING sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at death's door is departing life; something dying is fading out.

clue.text: Support beggar who's lost heart

indicators.note: the middle letters of the word beggar are dropped

explanation.surface: Help a pauper who has become disheartened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who's lost heart' removes the central GG.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear is to hold up or carry a weight, a synonym of support.

clue.text: Pancakes left in bin by yours truly

indicators.note: the letter for left goes inside the word bin

parts.note: the speaker referring to themselves, I

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to binning leftover pancakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Blini are small Russian buckwheat pancakes, often served with caviar.

clue.text: Deceive on more than one occasion

definitions.meaning: to cheat on a partner by seeing someone else

explanation.definitionFit: To two-time is to be unfaithful to a lover; literally it reads as two times.

clue.text: Yogurt occasionally available

indicators.note: only now and then, so every other letter of yogurt is taken

explanation.surface: Yogurt is on sale now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of yOgUrT.
explanation.definitionFit: A product that is out has been released and can be bought.

clue.text: Food soldiers may dig into?

parts.note: soldiers are British slang for strips of toast dipped into a soft-boiled yolk, not troops digging in

explanation.definitionFit: Toast soldiers are dunked into a soft-boiled one at breakfast in Britain.

clue.text: Overextend Her Majesty? She might be carried off on this

definitions.text: She might be carried off on this

parts.note: stretch means to extend too far
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's monogram

explanation.surface: Pushing the Queen too far might see her carried off.
explanation.definitionFit: Injured people are carried away on a stretcher, a portable bed.
